# Estima (01, engineer) — SPD-088

## Brief
Objective: the Bash hook must read an arithmetic command `(( ... ))` and an arithmetic expansion `$(( ... ))` as arithmetic, so a comparison inside one is never read as a redirection and never refused as a write to a file.

The bug. Both shells evaluate `(( ... ))` as arithmetic: the `>` inside it is a comparison and no file is opened. `zsh.mark_zsh_patterns` already recognises the region (the `text.startswith("((", i) and (command or arith_next)` branch near the top of its loop) and copies `text[i:end]` through verbatim into both readings -- so the `>` survives into `syntax.shell_tokens`, and `directories.separate_redirects` (bin/spudlib/shell/directories.py:30) reads it as an output operator and the next word as a target. `prepare.split_substitutions` deliberately skips `$((`, so an arithmetic expansion stays in the outer text and reaches the same reading.

Evidence, from analyse_command on the working tree at the time SPD-088 was filed: `(( 3 > 2 ))` records redirects ['2'], `if (( n > 2 )); then echo x; fi` ['2'], `x=$(( 1 > 2 ))` ['2'], `if (( i > 0 )); then true; fi` ['0'], `(( n >= 3 ))` ['='] and `(( a > b ))` ['b']; `let "n > 2"` and `[[ 3 -gt 2 ]]` record none. The SPD-049 differential shows `x=$(( 1<2 )); (( 3 > 2 )) && echo y` as one of 32 member lines that went silent -> deny. So a member writing `if (( retries > 3 )); then` is refused wherever the shell's directory is outside its deliverables, and so is Spud in a protected one.

The fix, as sketched on the ticket: mark the characters between `((` and `))`, and inside a `$(( ))` arithmetic expansion, the way mark_zsh_patterns already marks zsh's own glob operators -- a sentinel that shlex keeps inside a word and `prepare.deglob` restores -- so separate_redirects and ShellWalk never see an operator there. Reuse the existing sentinel machinery in `syntax.py` (`_ZSH_PATTERN_CHARS`, `_ZSH_SENTINELS`, `_SENTINEL_TEXT`, `_GLOB_SENTINEL_RE`, `_LITERALIZE`) rather than inventing a parallel one; add a sentinel only where an existing one cannot carry the meaning, and keep `deglob` a faithful inverse. Decide deliberately, and say in a comment, whether the marked region is one word or several -- the tests must pin whichever you choose.

Read first:
- `.claude/skills/spudlib-modules/SKILL.md` -- the rules bin/spudlib/ was built on: the import rule (a module imports modules, never names), where a module goes, what must stay off the hook path, the launcher's loader, and the size rule (~250 lines is a look-again point, never a cap).
- `bin/spudlib/shell/zsh.py` -- `mark_zsh_patterns`, `_scan_pairs`, `_zsh_group`; the `((` branch is where the region is already found.
- `bin/spudlib/shell/syntax.py` -- the sentinel tables and their contract, and the comment block above `_ZSH_PATTERN_CHARS`.
- `bin/spudlib/shell/prepare.py` -- `split_substitutions` (it skips `$((` on purpose), `neutralize_quoted_globs`, `deglob`.
- `bin/spudlib/shell/directories.py` -- `separate_redirects`, the reader that currently goes wrong.
- `bin/spudlib/shell/analyse.py` -- `analyse_command`: the two readings (zsh's `marked`, the other shell's `other`) and the `marked == plain` short circuit.
- `bin/spudlib/shell/walk.py` -- `ShellWalk`, so an arithmetic command still ends where it ends and a `for (( ... ))` header still opens its body.
- `tests/test_hooks.py` -- the existing analyse_command and member-denial tests; put yours beside their nearest neighbours in the file's own style.

Done when:
- Silent for a member whose shell directory is outside its deliverables, and recording no redirect target: `(( n > 2 ))`, `(( i > 0 ))`, `(( 3 > 2 ))`, `(( n >= 3 ))`, `(( a > b ))`, `if (( retries > 3 )); then echo x; fi`, `x=$(( 1 > 2 ))`, `x=$(( 1<2 )); (( 3 > 2 )) && echo y`.
- The other operators inside arithmetic are read as arithmetic too, not as shell punctuation: `(( n < 2 ))`, `(( n >> 1 ))`, `(( n << 1 ))`, `(( a && b ))`, `(( a || b ))`, `(( a | b ))`, `(( a & b ))`, `(( a > b ? 1 : 0 ))` -- none of them splits the line into more commands or opens a target.
- A `for (( i = 0; i < 10; i++ )); do ...; done` header is still a header: its body still runs in command position, its `<` opens nothing, and the loop still closes where it closed before.
- A real redirection is still checked, for a member and for Spud: `(( n > 2 )) > out.txt`, `(( n > 2 )) && echo x > out.txt`, `x=$(( 1 + 1 )) > out.txt`, and a target outside the deliverables is still refused with the same reason as before.
- Nothing that was refused before is silent now beyond arithmetic: `echo x > 2`, `echo x > b` and the SPD-045 descriptor forms behave exactly as they did.
- An unbalanced or unparseable `((` (no closing pair, `(( ` alone, `$(( 1 + ` ) is no crash and no new silence: the existing fallback stands, and a test pins it.
- Both readings still agree where they must -- an arithmetic command is arithmetic in bash and zsh alike, so `marked` and `other` carry the same marking and `analyse_command`'s second walk is not made to disagree with the first.
- New tests in `tests/test_hooks.py` pin every bullet above, including the ticket's own three (`(( n > 2 ))`, `(( n >= 3 ))`, `(( a > b ))` silent for a member) and a real redirection after an arithmetic command still checked.
- The full suite is green: `python3.14 -I -S -m unittest discover -s tests -t tests` (876 tests, about ten minutes) from the worktree root. You are the only member in this checkout, so the suite is yours alone (SPD-083); do not run two at once.
- The hook-timing probe passes within 1 ms of main -- these modules are all on the hook path: `python3.14 -I -S tests/probes/hook_timing.py 30 bin/spud /Users/ericlugo/Personal/Spud/bin/spud`.
- `python3.14 -I -S tests/probes/module_sizes.py` is advisory; if a module crosses ~250 lines say so in your Result rather than cutting a cohesive region to fit a number.

Notes:
- Work in this worktree (`.claude/worktrees/spd-088-arith-command`, branch `worktree-spd-088-arith-command`); all deliverable globs are relative to it.
- The launcher caches bytecode under `.spud/pycache/`; the suite handles it, but if a stale read ever confuses you, that is where to look.
- Keep the module docstrings and comment style of the files you touch: this code explains what was probed in which shell and why, and a new reading of `((` deserves the same treatment -- name what you probed, in which shell, if you probe.

## Log
- 2026-09-15T23:52 Reproduced SPD-088 on the worktree: analyse_command('(( n > 2 ))').redirects == ['2'], matching the ticket's evidence for all six recorded forms. Fix: syntax._ARITH_SENTINELS (0xE030+, inert -- GLOB_RE does not read them) plus the existing quoted-glob sentinels for *?[]{}, and _LITERAL_DOLLAR for $; zsh.mark_zsh_patterns marks the arithmetic in both its branches, the same text into both readings.
- 2026-09-15T23:56 Decision, pinned in tests and in the comment above the tables: the marked region is SEVERAL words for an arithmetic command and ONE for an arithmetic expansion. A command's outer parenthesis and its match stay real (ShellWalk opens and closes the frame it always did; its for-header scan still finds the end) and its blanks stay blanks, so a $( ... ) inside it is still analysed and stays out of the command word, where a substitution is a refusal; every character between the parentheses is marked, the inner ( of (( included, so the first word always starts with a sentinel and no word is read as a command name, a variable, an assignment or a glob. An expansion is marked whole, parentheses and blanks included, since it is part of a word.
- 2026-09-15T23:56 Trade recorded: (( x=1 )) no longer records x in the analysis's variables, since the region's first word is now behind a sentinel. Fails closed (a later $x refuses a member where it used to resolve to 1) and an arithmetic value is a number, never a command word or a path; pinned by test_an_arithmetic_assignment_is_no_longer_recorded. Gained with it: (( $n > 2 )), (( ${n} > 2 )) and if (( $retries > 3 )) are silent now, where the hook used to refuse them for a command word that does not exist.
- 2026-09-16T00:05 First full suite: 886 tests, 3 failures. Two were stale (the run had loaded the pre-edit test file). The real one: ParameterExpansionCommandWordTest pins '$((1)) push' as refused (SPD-043: the command word names a program the hook cannot read -- arithmetic yields a number, and a number can name an executable on a PATH of the line's own choosing), and marking the expansion's leading $ literal had silenced it. Fixed by marking only the $s inside the parentheses, never the one in front of them; '$((1)) push' and '$(( 1 + 1 ))' are refused again and pinned in the new class as a deliberate boundary.

## Ticket proposals
- **A spudagent in a worktree cannot probe a shell, so shell tickets have no fresh evidence** — suggested P3; open, with Spud.
  Why: The shell modules' comments are built on probes ('probed in zsh 5.9 -f -o nobareglobqual and bash 3.2'), and briefs for them ask for the same ('name what you probed, in which shell, if you probe'). A spudagent working a code ticket is in a worktree, and the worktree-isolation harness refuses every command that runs zsh or bash, script file included, because what the shell reads cannot be shown not to run git. So the one member who is reading the shells' grammar is the one member who cannot ask them, and its comments either cite older recorded evidence or go unevidenced. Either the briefs should stop asking, or there should be a way to ask.
  Evidence: SPD-088, this worktree: 'zsh -f -o nobareglobqual <scratchpad>/shellprobe.sh' and 'bash --version' were both refused with 'runs zsh in a plain command; what it reads or is handed as shell text cannot be shown not to run git'. The script only ran arithmetic forms in a mktemp directory. The new ArithmeticCommandTest docstring says so in as many words and rests on the ticket's own recorded analyse_command evidence instead, where every sibling class in tests/test_hooks.py (SPD-039, SPD-042, SPD-045, SPD-061) names a live probe.
